# `get_stacked_img`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Image socket: return the current stacked image as image bytes.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (scratch file on the raw path; 64-bit build, 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, imager binary image table (serves 4800/4804), handler @0x115ca0 (64-bit build), @0xa79b4 (32-bit build); static analysis of app 3.3.2, MainFileManager.getStackPic; GetStackImage(IMG_DATA&), shouldTransferJpg/convertImageToJpg, unconditional compression on the raw path, reponse_result; JPEG path, convertImageToJpg passes an empty target path to IMG_DATA::ToJPG, whose imwrite/Save branches run only for a non-empty path (CFG check, 64-bit build); raw path (unconditional), IMG_DATA::Compress @0x6a2d10 (64-bit) / @0x67236c (32-bit), WriteFile of a scratch file, run_popen of a zip command, ReadFile, remove |

Image-socket (4800/4804) method. Under a lock the handler copies the current stacked image into a request-local buffer and sends it: JPEG (imgType 4) in Jpg mode (error text `convert jpg failed` if conversion fails), otherwise always zip-compressed raw (dataType 3). READ. It reads an already-produced image; it does not recompute it or mutate shared state. The raw path always goes through a temporary scratch file on device storage, so under the strict convention it is a MUTATOR with observation-safe (tier B) effects. The 32-bit build matches (READ), apart from log wording and image-library version. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit): when the preview setting raw_bin2 is true, raw 16-bit Bayer (imgType 1) and RGB48 (imgType 5) frames on the non-JPEG path are binned 2x2 before sending; the header width, height and bytes 20 to 23 are halved and imgType is unchanged (READ; 32-bit not checked).

Side effects: Copies the stacked image into a request-local buffer under a mutex, converts it to JPEG or zip-compresses it, then responds with the bytes. No shared-state mutation or hardware access. READ; the 32-bit build matches (READ). JPEG conversion encodes in memory: the conversion routine writes a file only when it is given a target path, and this handler passes none. READ (64-bit build; the 32-bit build has the same call structure, READ). On the raw path (always compressed): zip compression of raw output writes the raw bytes to a fixed-name scratch file in the imager's private data directory, runs an external zip compressor on it, reads the archive back and deletes both files before replying. READ. Nothing persists, so the effect is observation-safe (tier B), but the handler is a MUTATOR under the strict convention, as for get_server_log. Because the scratch name is fixed, two compressed raw requests served at the same time could interfere; INFERRED.
